Rashi on Shabbat 37a:11:1.english: That was completely heated - For there is no concern of stoking [the coals].

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:1:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך להחזיר תנן - ואילו לשהות, אע"פ שאינו גרוף, שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:1:1.english: Actually, I can say to you [that] we learned "to return" - Whereas leaving [food on the stove], even though [the stove] is not swept, is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:1:2.hebrew: והך חזרה דאמרי לך - "לא יחזיר עד שיגרוף", דכי גרוף מיהא שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:1:2.english: And that return that I said to you - "One may not return [it] until one sweeps," for once [it is] swept, at least, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:1:3.english: Is not according to everyone - And Beit Shammai do not hold [this view].

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:1.hebrew: לא שנו - שריותא דמתני', אלא על גבה, דלא נפיש הבלא כולי האי; אבל תוכה — אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:1.english: They only taught - the permission of the Mishnah [applies] only atop it, as the heat is not so great; but inside it is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:2.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא להחזיר תנן - אבל לשהות משהין אפילו בשאין גרופה, כדמחסרינן ליה חסורי — ורבי חלבו אשריותא דלשהות על שאינה גרופה קאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:2.english: Granted, if you say that we learned returning - but as for leaving, one may leave [food] even when [the stove] is not swept, as we emended [the Mishnah by stating that] it is missing [text]; and Rabbi Ḥelbo refers to the permission to leave [food] on [a stove] that is not swept.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:3.hebrew: היינו דשני בין תוכה לעל גבה - דכי משהי לתוכה דשאינה גרופה, מטמין ממש ברמץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:3.english: That is why there is a difference between inside it and atop it - For when one leaves [food] inside [a stove] that is not swept, he is literally insulating [it] in hot ashes.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:4.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת לשהות תנן - דאפילו לשהות בעי גרופה, כיון דגרופה, ומבעוד יום הוא נותנו לתוכה — מה לי תוכה, מה לי על גבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:4.english: However, if you say we learned "to leave" - That even to leave [food on the stove] requires [the stove to be] swept; [and] since it is swept, and while it is still day he places it inside it, what is [the difference] to me [whether it is] inside it, [and] what is [the difference] to me [whether it is] atop it?

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:5.english: To the first clause - [Namely,] "until he sweeps [it] out."

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:6.hebrew: אסיפא קאי - דאיירי בחזרה, אבל רישא לשהות הוא, ובין תוכה ובין גבה שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:2:6.english: [He] is referring to the latter clause - Which deals with returning; but the first clause is [about] leaving, and both inside it and atop it are permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:3:1.hebrew: שתי כירות המתאימות - מחוברות יחד, וקיר של חרס מפסקת ביניהם:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:3:1.english: Two adjoining stoves - Joined together, and an earthenware wall separates between them.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:3:2.english: One may leave [food] atop [the one that was] swept or covered with ashes - For we are not concerned that heat rises to it from the other [stove].

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:3:3.english: And what may one leave? - On the swept [stove].

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:3:4.english: One may not return [it] - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:1.hebrew: אא"ב - רישא דמתניתין לשהות קאמר, דבעי גרופה, ובלשהות פליגי בחמין ובתבשיל ובגרוף, וסיפא פליגי בחזרה — מתני' ר' יהודה היא. אלא אי אמרת להחזיר תנן, דבעי גרופה, אבל לשהות לא בעי גרופה, ופלוגתא דחמין ותבשיל כשאינו גרוף, כדקמחסרת ומתרצת לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:1.english: Granted, if you say - The first clause of our Mishnah is speaking of leaving [a pot on the stove], [teaching] that it requires [the stove to be] swept; and regarding leaving [on a stove that is] swept, they disagree about hot water and cooked food; and in the latter clause they disagree about returning [a pot to the stove] — [in that case,] our Mishnah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda. However, if you say that we learned [that it is with regard to] returning that requires [the stove to be] swept, but leaving does not require [it to be] swept, and the dispute concerning hot water and cooked food is when it is not swept, as you emended and explained it:

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:2.hebrew: קשיא לב"ש בחדא - דקאמרי ב"ש במתני': משהין חמין אף בשאינו גרוף, והכא קאמר רבי מאיר לב"ש דאפילו גרוף — ולא כלום, וכ"ש כשאינו גרוף. והא כולה חדא פירכא היא, דבית שמאי לא שני להו בין גרוף לשאינו גרוף:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:2.english: It is difficult for Beit Shammai in one [respect] - For Beit Shammai say in our Mishnah: One may leave hot water [on the stove] even when it is not swept; whereas here, Rabbi Meir says regarding Beit Shammai that even [if it is] swept, [one may leave] nothing at all, and all the more so when it is not swept. And this entire [difficulty] is a single refutation, since Beit Shammai do not differentiate between [a stove that is] swept and [one that is] not swept.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:3.hebrew: ולב"ה בתרתי - דבמתניתין שרי בית הלל להשהות חמין ותבשיל אף בשאינו גרוף, והכא קתני דבגרוף — חמין אין, תבשיל לא, ובשאינה גרוף — אין משהין כלל. ולענין חזרה בגרוף — תנן במתניתין: לב"ה מחזירין, והכא קתני: עקר — דברי הכל לא יחזיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:3.english: And for Beit Hillel in two [respects] - For in our Mishnah, Beit Hillel permit leaving hot water and cooked food even on [a stove] that is not swept, whereas here it teaches that on a swept [stove], hot water, yes, [but] cooked food, no, and on [a stove] that is not swept, one may not leave [anything] at all. And regarding returning [a pot] on a swept [stove], we learned in our Mishnah: According to Beit Hillel, one may return [it], whereas here it teaches: [If] one removed [it], all agree that he may not return [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:4.hebrew: ואי ר' יהודה - דאמר נמי כי מתניתין, מ"מ גרופה וקטומה קשיא — דמתניתין תרצת דפלוגתא קמייתא בשאינו גרוף, ושרו ב"ש חמין ובית הלל חמין ותבשיל; והכא קתני: אין משהין על גבי שאינה גרופה ואינה קטומה כלל, ופלוגתא דלשהות — בגרופה וקטומה:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:4:4.english: And if Rabbi Yehuda - [Even though] he also says in accordance with our mishna, nevertheless, [the matter of] swept and covered is difficult — for you explained our mishna [such] that the first dispute is regarding [a stove] that is not swept, and Beit Shammai permit hot water and Beit Hillel [permit] hot water and cooked food; whereas here [in the baraita] it teaches: One may not leave [anything] atop [a stove] that is neither swept nor covered [with ashes] at all, and the dispute regarding leaving is on [a stove that is] swept and covered.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:5:1.hebrew: בחמין ותבשיל ונוטלים ומחזירין - דמוקי פלוגתא דב"ש וב"ה בשהיית חמין ותבשיל, דבית שמאי שרו חמין, ותבשיל לא, וב"ה — חמין ותבשיל; ולא כר' מאיר, דאמר: לב"ש לא כלום:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:5:1.english: Regarding hot water and cooked food, and [that] they may take and return - For he establishes the dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel concerning the leaving of hot water and cooked food [as being] that Beit Shammai permit hot water, but not cooked food, and Beit Hillel [permit both] hot water and cooked food; and not like Rabbi Meir, who said that according to Beit Shammai, nothing at all [may be left].

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:6:1.hebrew: מהו לסמוך - קדרה אצל דופן הכירה בלא גרופה — שהכירה מטלטלת היא, ומושיבים אותה על גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Shabbat 37a:6:1.english: What is [the law regarding] leaning - [Leaning] a pot against the wall of the stove when [it is] not swept [of coals] — for the stove is portable, and they set it on the ground:

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:6:2.english: Its top - The thickness of its rim, or a cover that is over its cavity.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:7:1.english: That it is elevated - The pot atop the stove.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:8:1.english: And it reignited - It caught fire again.

Rashi on Shabbat 37a:9:1.english: There, removing and returning are in one place - And it is not appropriate to teach [about] returning until it teaches [about] removing.

Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:10:1.hebrew: תא שמע כירה שהסיקוה כו' - ומסיק דשרי לסמוך. ומכל מקום, אין ללמוד מכאן לסמוך אצל האש, דשאני הכא, דדופני כירה מפסיקין בינו ולאש:
Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:10:1.english: "Come and hear: A stove that was lit," etc. - And [the Gemara] concludes that it is permitted to lean [food against it]. Nevertheless, one cannot learn from here [that it is permitted] to lean [food] next to the fire, for it is different here, as the walls of the stove intervene between it and the fire.

Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:1:1.hebrew: לעולם אימא לך להחזיר תנן וחסורי מיחסרא כו' - משום דקיי"ל כחנניה, כמו שאפרש בע"ה, דחיק לאוקמא מתני' כוותיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:1:1.english: "Actually, I could say to you: We learned 'to return', and it is missing [text], etc." - Because we hold in accordance with Chananyah — as I will explain with the help of God — [the Gemara] strains to establish the Mishnah in accordance with his view.

Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:2:1.hebrew: אא"ב להחזיר תנן היינו דשני בין תוכה לעל גבה - פי' בקונטרס: משום דאי "להחזיר" תנן, א"כ לשהות משהין אפילו באינה גרופה; להכי שני בין תוכה — דהוי מטמין ממש ברמץ — לעל גבה. וקשה להר"ח: דלחנניה אפילו תוכה משהין, אפי' באינה גרופה, דהא תנן (. לעיל שבת דף יט:) "ולא חררה על גבי גחלים אלא עד שיקרמו פניה", הא קרמו פניה שרי, אע"ג דחררה בתוכה היא! ובלאו הכי, אור"י דבחנם דחק רש"י לפרש כן, דאיכא למימר שפיר: "היינו דשני לן בין תוכה לעל גבה" מהא דשרי להחזיר בגרופה; ובהשהאה דוקא לא ניחא ליה לחלק, אבל בהחזרה ניחא ליה שפיר לחלק, כדמוכח במאי דמשני: "מי סברת ארישא קאי? אסיפא קאי" כו'. קשה לר"י: היכי בעי למימר אליבא דרב דמתניתין "להחזיר" תנן? אם כן, אתיא מתניתין כחנניה, ורב דלא כחנניה! דהא חנניה שרי במצטמק ויפה לו, דהא דתנן (שם) "אין צולין בשר וביצה אלא כדי שיצולו מבעוד יום" אתיא כחנניה, וביצה אמרינן לקמן דמצטמק ויפה לו הוא, ורב אסר לקמן דמצטמק ויפה לו! וי"ל, דבלאו הכי לא סבר לה רב כשום תנא, דהא ר"מ ור' יהודה אסרי באינה גרופה אפילו במצטמק ורע לו, ורב שרי במצטמק ורע לו אפילו באינה גרופה — דבגרופה לא אשכחן שום אמורא דאסר אפילו יפה לו. ועוד, דרב קאי אמילתיה דרבי יוחנן דאיירי באינה גרופה; וכן רבי יוחנן, דשרי לקמן חמין ותבשיל שבישל כל צרכו באינה גרופה, אבל לא בישל כל צרכו אסור — לא אשכחן תנא דסבר הכי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:2:1.english: Granted, if you say that we learned "to return", that is why there is a difference between inside it and atop it - The Kuntras [Rashi] explained that if we learned "to return", then if so, leaving [food on the stove] is permitted even on an unswept [stove]; therefore, [Rabbi Ḥelbo] distinguished between inside it — where one is literally insulating in hot ashes — and atop it. And this is difficult to Rabbeinu Ḥananel, for according to Ḥananyah, one may leave [food] even inside it, even on an unswept [stove]! For we learned (. above, Shabbat 19b): "Nor [may one place] a cake upon coals unless its crust has formed." Thus, [once] its crust has formed, it is permitted, even though a cake is inside it! And regardless of this, Ri says that Rashi needlessly strained himself to explain this so, for one can well say: "That is why there is a difference between inside it and atop it" is from that which it is permitted to return on a swept [stove]; and it was specifically with regard to leaving that it was not satisfactory to [the Gemara] to distinguish [between inside and atop], but with regard to returning, it was well satisfactory to [the Gemara] to distinguish, as is proven from that which it answers: "Do you think that he refers to the first clause? He refers to the latter clause, etc." Ri asks: How could [the Gemara] want to say, according to Rav, that we learned "to return" in the mishnah? If so, the mishnah follows Ḥananyah, and Rav does not [hold] like Ḥananyah! For Ḥananyah permits [leaving food that] shrinks and improves — for that which we learned (ibid.): "One may not roast meat or an egg unless they can roast while it is still day," follows Ḥananyah, and with regard to an egg, we say below [38a] that it shrinks and improves, whereas Rav forbids below [food that] shrinks and improves! And one can say that regardless of this, Rav does not hold like any Tanna [here]. For Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah forbid on an unswept [stove] even [food that] shrinks and deteriorates, whereas Rav permits [food that] shrinks and deteriorates even on an unswept [stove] — for on a swept [stove], we do not find any Amora who forbids even [food that] improves. And furthermore, Rav is addressing the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan, which deals with an unswept [stove]; and similarly Rabbi Yoḥanan, who permits below [leaving] hot water and cooked food that was completely cooked on an unswept [stove], but if it was not completely cooked it is forbidden — we do not find a Tanna who holds like this.

Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:6:1.hebrew: מהו לסמוך - באינה גרופה קבעי. ואי מתניתין להשהות תנן, קא בעי להשהות ולהחזיר; ואי להחזיר תנן, ושרי להשהות אפי' תוכה וגבה — בעי להחזיר, ולהשהות היכא שאינו מבושל כמאכל בן דרוסאי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 37a:6:1.english: What is [the halakha regarding] leaning [against it] - It is asking regarding [a stove that is] not swept. And if in our Mishnah we learned [the prohibition with regard] to leaving [food before Shabbat], it is asking regarding [both] leaving and returning; and if we learned [it with regard] to returning, and [thus] it is permitted to leave [food] even inside it and on top of it, it is asking regarding returning, and regarding leaving where [the food] is not cooked like the food of ben Derosai.
